newsitem.title: USA: SEC charges Montedison with acctg fraud.
newsitem.headline: SEC charges Montedison with acctg fraud.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Comnission said Thursday it charged the Italian conglomerate Montedison SpA with accounting fraud for allegedly falsifying data to artifically inflate its financial condition.

In a civil complaint filed in federal district court here, the SEC said it also charged Montedison with violating corporate reporting, books and records and internal control regulations under U.S. federal securities law.

The stock of the Milan-based conglomerate, which operates agro-industry, chemical, energy and engineering businesses, is traded as American Depositary Shares on the New York Stock Exchange since July 1987. As such, it files financial statements, including annual reports, with the SEC.

The SEC alleged that Montedison violated antifraud provisions of securities law "by engaging in a fraudulent scheme to materially misstate its financial condition and results of its operations" on reports filed with the agency. The "fraudulent scheme" continued from at least 1988 through the first half of 1993, the SEC alleged.

The scheme was designed to conceal hundreds of millions of dollars of payments that were used to bribe politicians in Italy and other persons, resulting in hidden losses of at least $398 million, the SEC alleged.
As part of the scheme, the SEC alleged Montedison's assets were materially overstated on its books and records for the 1988, 1989, 1990 and 1991 fiscal years.
The SEC alleged that from December 1988 to May 1993, numerous undocumented payments running into hundreds of millions of dollars were made by the company or its agents.

In one case, the SEC alleged that Montedison fictitiously "loaned" about $272 million to a Curacao, Netherlands Antilles, unit that then funnelled the money to Exilar International SA, a British Virgin Islands firm.
In the later half of 1993, Montedison decided the loan was "uncollectible" and took a writedown of the whole amount for its 1992 fiscal year, the SEC alleged.

The SEC also alleged Montedison arranged with a Rome developer to effect real estate deals at artificially high prices. The developer then used the money to bribe Italian politicos and other persons on Montedison's behalf, the agency alleged.

Montedison's goal in this scheme, the SEC alleged, was to gain control of Enimont, a joint venture with the Italian state energy company ENI SpA. At the time, a Milan judge had frozen ENI's and Montedison's shares in the joint venture and gave custody and voting rights to a third party, the SEC said.

The SEC alleged that the overstated real estate deals were used to disguise the bribes on the company's books from 1990 to 1992. This resulted later in a writedown on the comnpany's 1993 financial statements of about $126.25 million, it alleged.
